python.note: Most often "Python" means a programming language: "She writes code in Python."
ex: The python at the zoo is longer than a car.
A python is a big snake that squeezes its food.
Is that python dangerous to small children?
The python is sleeping under a warm lamp.
Blogging is a good way to share your ideas.
She makes some extra money from blogging about food.
Blogging became her full-time job last year.
Is blogging still popular with young people?
He wears a turban to work every day.
The man in the blue turban is my teacher.
She tied a long scarf around her head like a turban.
Many Sikh men wear a turban in public.
Our beagle loves to smell everything on walks.
A beagle is a friendly dog for families.
Is your beagle good with small children?
The beagle barks loudly when someone is at the door.
We use a kerosene lamp when the power goes out.
This old heater in the garage runs on kerosene.
Kerosene has a very strong smell.
Where can I buy kerosene for my camping stove?
Doctors once used ether to put patients to sleep.
Ether has a strong smell and burns very easily.
Keep the bottle of ether away from fire.
The chemist poured some ether into a glass flask.

moo.note: Usually a sound word; also used as a verb: "the cows mooed".

engineering.note: Most often "engineering" is the science and job of engineers: "She studies engineering."
ex: The company offers engineering services for new factories.
We hired a firm to do the engineering for the new bridge.
Can your company do the engineering for this project?
The engineering costs were higher than we planned.

bridge.note: Most often "bridge" means a road over a river: "We walked across the bridge."

creme.note: Mostly used in French food names like "creme brulee"; otherwise say "cream."

squash.note: Most often "squash" is a vegetable like a pumpkin: "We cooked squash for dinner."
ex: We play squash twice a week after work.
Squash is a fast sport that people play indoors.
Can I book a squash court for Friday evening?
You need a racket and a small ball for squash.

lackey.note: Insulting word for a person who obeys others too much.

paintball.note: Uncountable for the game: "play paintball"; one shot is a "paintball" too.
ex: We played paintball for my birthday last weekend.
Paintball can hurt if you don't wear protection.
Do you want to play paintball with us on Saturday?
The team went to a paintball park outside the city.
We often play badminton in the backyard in summer.
She is on the school badminton team this year.
Badminton is very popular in many Asian countries.
Can I borrow your badminton racket this weekend?
He plays sax in the school jazz band.
The sax solo in this song is amazing.
She carries her sax to practice every Tuesday.
Can you play the sax, or only the piano?

khaki.note: Uncountable as a color; "khakis" means pants.
ex: The soldiers were dressed in khaki from head to toe.
Khaki is a good color for hiking clothes.
Do you have this jacket in khaki or black?
He bought a light jacket in khaki for the trip.
The church teaches this idea as dogma.
He refused to accept any political dogma.
Some old dogmas are slowly changing today.
Good scientists question dogma and test their ideas.
I made fettuccine alfredo for dinner tonight.
The alfredo sauce here is rich and creamy.
Can I get the chicken alfredo without mushrooms?
You make alfredo with butter, cream, and cheese.
The magnolia in our yard is blooming again.
Magnolia flowers have a sweet, strong smell.
She planted a pink magnolia near the house.
Is that big tree with white flowers a magnolia?

proponent.note: Formal word; "supporter" is more common in everyday speech.

ex: The app uses a free weather API.
Developers can connect to our API with a key.
The API sends the data back in JSON.
Please read the API documentation before you start.
We drank tea on the veranda after dinner.
The house has a wide veranda in front.
They sat on the veranda and watched the rain.
Can we eat outside on the veranda today?

vocal.note: Usually "vocals" for the singing in a song; "vocal" is often an adjective: "vocal cords."

mustang.note: Most often "Mustang" is the name of a sports car; "a mustang" is a wild horse.

ex: We saw a geisha walking in the old part of town.
A geisha entertains guests with music and dance.
Geishas usually wear beautiful kimonos and white makeup.
She read a book about a geisha's life in Japan.

artiste.note: Often humorous; in daily speech say "artist" or "performer."
